performed_via_github_app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (2) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. IPv6 server names break 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>Flask.run splits SERVER_NAME at the first colon, so a bracketed IPv6 value such as [::1]:8080
>produces host [ and nonnumeric port :1]:8080. With default arguments this raises ValueError,
>while an explicit port causes the server to bind using the invalid host [ instead of ::1.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/flask/app.py[724]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/pull/6208/files#diff-d3e0349504081bb501c611b3954be364188a4cf442056181272e27e830ae446eR724-R724) > >```diff >+ sn_host, _, sn_port = server_name.partition(":") >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>SERVER_NAME is documented as the host and port to which the application is bound. The changed
>parser feeds its first component into the host default and converts the remainder to an integer port
>before passing both values to run_simple; the existing tests confirm these configured defaults are
>public behavior but cover only DNS hostnames.
>
> > [src/flask/app.py[720-737]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/331791a7e7d818437d81078c399847a5b692f114/src/flask/app.py/#L720-L737) > [src/flask/app.py[745-748]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/331791a7e7d818437d81078c399847a5b692f114/src/flask/app.py/#L745-L748) > [docs/config.rst[279-287]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/331791a7e7d818437d81078c399847a5b692f114/docs/config.rst/#L279-L287) > [tests/test_basic.py[1906-1927]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/331791a7e7d818437d81078c399847a5b692f114/tests/test_basic.py/#L1906-L1927) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`Flask.run` no longer correctly parses bracketed IPv6 `SERVER_NAME` values because `str.partition(":")` treats an IPv6 address colon as the host-port delimiter. > >## Issue Context >Restore authority-aware parsing that extracts the complete IPv6 hostname and optional port. Add coverage for bracketed IPv6 values both with and without an explicit port, including cases where the `host` or `port` argument overrides the configured value. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/flask/app.py[720-737] >- tests/test_basic.py[1906-1927] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
2. IPv6 session cookies disappear 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>session_transaction derives the cookie host with ctx.request.host.partition(":")[0], which
>returns [ for an IPv6 authority such as [::1]:5000. The saved session cookie is therefore
>associated with the wrong host and is not sent on a subsequent request to the IPv6 URL, losing the
>transaction's session changes.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/flask/testing.py[180]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/pull/6208/files#diff-8b6ebc456dd7ce1ab0df544ee20d38211b947ad84e600b2727e4dd5db9fe913eR180-R180) > >```diff >+ ctx.request.host.partition(":")[0], >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The test request builder accepts an explicit URL authority and preserves it in the request. After
>saving the session, the changed line passes the incorrectly partitioned host to Werkzeug's cookie
>update operation, while the session transaction contract tested elsewhere requires those cookies to
>persist into later client requests.
>
> > [src/flask/testing.py[65-79]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/331791a7e7d818437d81078c399847a5b692f114/src/flask/testing.py/#L65-L79) > [src/flask/testing.py[160-182]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/331791a7e7d818437d81078c399847a5b692f114/src/flask/testing.py/#L160-L182) > [tests/test_testing.py[157-171]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/331791a7e7d818437d81078c399847a5b692f114/tests/test_testing.py/#L157-L171) > [src/flask/sessions.py[369-384]](https://github.com/seonho12-54/qodo-coderabbit-benchmark/blob/331791a7e7d818437d81078c399847a5b692f114/src/flask/sessions.py/#L369-L384) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`session_transaction` stores response cookies against `[` rather than the actual hostname when the request uses a bracketed IPv6 authority. > >## Issue Context >Use URL-aware hostname extraction that removes IPv6 brackets and excludes the optional port. Add a session transaction test that saves and retrieves session data using the same IPv6 `base_url`. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/flask/testing.py[160-182] >- tests/test_testing.py[157-171] >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
